raw_response:
Aiya, you want to know how I'll manage my cotton this year? Let me think... I've been growing cotton on this little patch for so many years, my hands know what to do before my head does.

My two mu of cotton — that's all I have. My sons and daughter work outside, in the city mostly, so it's just me and the old man on the land now. We're not young anymore, my back hurts when I bend too long. But cotton, I know cotton. My mother grew cotton, I grew cotton when I came to this village as a bride, and I'm still growing cotton.

**When to plant?** Around Guyu (谷雨), maybe a few days after — when the ground is warm enough that if I stick my hand in, it doesn't feel cold. The old people say wait until the apricot trees finish flowering. Usually that's the end of April, around the 20th or so. If it's a cold spring I wait longer. No use planting into cold ground, the seeds just sit there and rot.

**What seed?** I buy seed from the same shop in town every year. The boss there knows me. Whatever everyone in the village is using — I think it's some hybrid kind, the bag has pictures on it but I can't read what it says. My nephew reads it for me when I ask. Costs maybe 30-40 yuan for what I need for two mu. I don't save my own seed anymore, the new kinds don't grow right if you save them, that's what people say.

**Fertilizer.** Before I plant, I spread some compound fertilizer — the kind with three numbers on the bag, the shop owner picks it for me. Maybe two bags for my two mu, that's about 50 jin (25 kg) per mu, I just spread it by hand and rake it in. Then when the cotton is about knee-high and starts to bud, I put down some urea — maybe 20 jin per mu, scatter it around the plants before a rain or before I water. If the leaves look pale, I do it again later. I don't measure with scales, I measure with the scoop in the bag. Two scoops per mu of urea, that's how I learned it.

**Watering.** We have the well, but the water costs money — the electricity. I water before planting if the ground is dry, then once when the cotton is budding, and once when the bolls are filling out. Three times usually. If it rains good I skip one. The well water is expensive but cotton without water in dry years gives nothing.

**Pests and weeds.** Cotton has bollworm trouble. I walk through every few days to look at the leaves and the buds. If I see the worms or the holes, I spray. The shop sells the medicine in small bottles, mix it with water in the sprayer on my back. I do herbicide once when the weeds start, sometimes I just hoe by hand because it's only two mu, my old man and I can manage. Aphids sometimes too, I spray for those.

**Tilling.** My neighbor's son has a small tractor, he plows my land for me — I give him a little money or some vegetables from my garden. Just one plowing in spring. Nothing complicated.

**Picking.** This is the hard part now that I'm old. Cotton doesn't all open at once, you go through the field three, four times from September into October, picking the open bolls. My daughter comes back from the city for a week sometimes to help. If she can't come, I hire one or two women from the village for a few days, pay them by the day or by the jin picked. My back can't do it all alone like before.

**How much will I get?** Last year wasn't bad — maybe 250 jin of seed cotton per mu? The year before that the bollworm was bad and I only got 200. I hope for 250-280 per mu this year if heaven gives good weather. The price... whatever the buyers come and offer in autumn. We don't have a choice, you sell when they come.

I don't make much from this little piece of land. But it's what I do. The children send money sometimes. The cotton money buys me my medicines and the new year things for the grandchildren.
